text:
maya: Heads-up: seeing missing trace IDs for some requests in eu-west1 after the node reboots earlier. Kibana searches for trace_id:abc123 return nothing. Anyone else?

raj: I saw a spike in pod restarts around 02:14 UTC. kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total shows ~120 restarts on gpu-pool-2. Could be upstream NAT swap.

lina: Are we sure it's an ingestion issue vs query window? Any correlating Loki hits? :eyes: 

maya: Quick Loki probe I ran (rough):
```
{cluster=\"eu-west1\"} |= \"trace_id=\" |~ \"trace_id=([a-z0-9]{6,})\"
| json
| trace_id!=\"\"
| count_over_time({cluster=\"eu-west1\"}[1h])
```
Got counts for request_id but trace_id field often empty.

tom: FYI the nginx-ingress proxy had a header rewrite bug last week where X-Request-Id gets replaced on conntrack reset. If the TCP socket flips, headers can be lost before the sidecar attaches them.

infra-bot: alert: high restart rate on gpu-pool-2 at 2025-11-12T02:14:21Z

raj: If proxy replaces the header, trace_id might never reach the log-enricher. Can we tcpdump on one host and confirm header sequence? Also check the sidecar enricher logs for dropped events.

lina: Can someone run this Kibana query for a sample request: `trace_id: \"abc123\" OR request_id: \"req-9876\"` and expand the time window +/-10m? 

maya: Ran it. Found request_id (req-9876) present in nginx access logs and the app logs, but trace_id (abc123) absent in Loki ingestion. The sidecar shows it received logs but with trace_id field empty. Looks like header didn't make it through the proxy to the sidecar.

tom: Opened ticket with provider — they confirmed a NAT gateway instance was flapping (conntrack entries reset on port churn). They've pushed a firmware patch to keep ephemeral ports stable across short reassignments.

raj: Short-term workaround: enrich logs at the app side with both request_id and a local generated span id before sending to the sidecar. Also increase Loki capture for the affected pool to avoid sampling away the few matching traces during the window.

lina: We should also tune alerts: bump the "missing-traceid-rate" threshold from 0.01 to 0.05 over 5m during infra events to reduce noise. And add a SLO dashboard panel showing request_id vs trace_id ratio per region.

maya: I'll prepare a canary: sidecar will add header `x-local-span` and we'll update the log parser to prefer trace_id then x-local-span. PR incoming for parser change and a small Grafana panel.

tom: I'll coordinate with provider to confirm the patch and follow up. Also adding a Grafana mute rule that auto-silences the missing-traceid alert for 30m if a node-pool rolling-update or provider maintenance flag is detected.

maya: Assigning follow-ups: @raj to patch parser/enricher, @lina to update alert and dashboard, @tom to chase provider. I'll take the postmortem once provider confirms fix. :thumbsup:

raj: on it.

lina: updated draft alert rule (dashboard link placeholder): https://grafana.redwood/alert/123

infra-bot: ticket #CL-4421 created with provider. Status: investigating

alert-bot: Note: I'll auto-silence missing-traceid alerts for the affected node-pool while ticket CL-4421 is open.
thread_summary: Investigation of missing trace_id fields in eu-west1 logs after node reboots; traced to NAT gateway/conntrack resets and proxy header rewrite. Actions: add local span enrichment, update parser, tune alerts, provider patch and ticket CL-4421.
